raw.cause: logger serves a channel created with ChannelCreate(_NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY), so its receiving thread keeps its own low priority instead of inheriting display's priority 30. Its 2 ms of work in logger_handle is preempted by media, a priority-20 CPU hog that runs 45 ms bursts on every CPU. display stays REPLY-blocked for about 45-50 ms (e.g. receive 3375.5 → reply 3423.7). In other cases the logger thread had not yet returned to MsgReceive, so display sat SEND-blocked for about 45 ms (4906.3 → 4951.6) and then got its reply 2 ms later. This is priority inversion, not slow logging code.
raw.qnx_call: ChannelCreate with _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY in logger (run_logger); display's MsgSend to logger waits behind media
raw.fix_summary: Drop _NTO_CHF_FIXED_PRIORITY from the logger channel so logger inherits the priority of the waiting client and runs ahead of media. COCKPIT_FIXED=1 already does this; make it unconditional. If logging really must never compete with real work, change the contract instead: display should not wait synchronously on logger. Have it log from a separate low-priority thread or send a pulse (MsgSendPulse) rather than calling MsgSend in the draw loop.
